html:
The Korubo are a small, largely uncontacted Panoan people of the Javari valley in the far west of the Brazilian Amazon, near the border with Peru. Portuguese speakers call them caceteiros, "clubbers", after the heavy war clubs they carry.

They live by hunting, fishing and farming forest gardens. For decades they clashed with loggers and fishermen, and deaths on both sides led the Brazilian agency for Indigenous peoples to make contact with one group in 1996, under the explorer Sydney Possuelo. Other Korubo groups were contacted in 2014, 2015 and 2019, while some still avoid outsiders. The Javari valley holds more uncontacted groups than anywhere else on earth. Their neighbours include the Matsés and the Marubo, in the far west of Brazil.
